shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C — reducing variety and going to zero in one good. Since I value variety, this decreases my utility rather than improving it.

Currently I have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. This trade would give me 2×A and 0×B, creating imbalance and leaving me with none of a good, which reduces variety-driven utility. Rejecting to preserve balance.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with A:3, B:0, C:1 — losing all variety in B, which I value highly due to diminishing returns on A. This decreases my overall utility rather than increasing it.

Current inventory is balanced at 1 each. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and thus utility. I'd rather keep balanced holdings unless the trade improves diversity.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

I have 0 B and 2 A, 2 C. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me from (2,0,2) to (1,1,2), increasing variety balance and overall utility since B was my scarcest good.
Giving up all my A (2 units) for just 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 2 C - too skewed and costly. I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade of A for B to maintain balance and variety.

Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so B is more valuable to me due to variety preference. Trading away 1 C (going from 2 to 1) for 1 B (going from 0 to 1) balances my inventory to 2A/1B/1C, increasing overall utility.

This would leave me with A:2, B:1, C:0, eliminating C entirely and creating a new imbalance. Giving up 2C for 1B is too steep - I'd rather get 1B for 1C to maintain more balance across all three goods.

Current inventory is A:2, B:0, C:1 — heavily skewed away from B. Trading 1 A (which I have 2 of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more balanced bundle (A:1, B:1, C:1), increasing utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading away all of one good for equal amount of another is too costly. I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to balance my inventory (2A,1B,1C would be nice, or even trade toward 1,1,1 first). This exact trade over-concentrates loss of A while I still want some A left."

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading away my only C for B would just swap which good I have zero of, not improving variety - I'd go from (2,0,1) to (2,1,0), same imbalance profile. Since C is already scarce for me, giving it away for another scarce good doesn't clearly help; I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that gives me B without losing my only C, or negotiate a better ratio.
Currently I have 0 B, 2 A, 2 C. Trading away 1 A (leaving 1) for 1 B (gaining my first) moves me toward a balanced 1-1-2 bundle, increasing variety utility since B was my scarcest good.

Trading A (I have 2) for B (I have 0) improves variety balance: resulting inventory A1/B1/C1 is more even and valuable under my variety-preferring utility than A2/B0/C1.

Since B and C are equally valued and I have 0 B and 1 C, trading 1 C for 1 B keeps total variety the same (2 distinct goods) but shifts which one - net neutral. Given no clear improvement, but this diversifies away from having zero B while now having zero C - equal tradeoff, so slight preference to accept to test market and eventually collect all three types starting now.
